properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 1 at 5:46AM MST until November 1 at 2:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 245 PM MST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of creeks and normally dry washes is imminent or
occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 545 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area. Between
1.5 and 2.25 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Ash Creek, Willow Creek, Miller Creek, Lynx Creek, Butte Creek,
Turkey Creek, Wolf Creek, Little Chino Valley, Big Bug Creek,
Agua Fria River, Bottleneck Wash, Milk Creek, Granite Creek,
Verde River, Bannon Creek and Hassayampa River. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned
area.
- For Granite Creek at Prescott:
At 5:30am the stage was 11.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Flooding begins at AC Williams Granite Creek Park
upstream of gage. Low lying patios along Granite Creek in
downtown Prescott flood.
- For Granite Creek at Granite Creek Near Prescott:
At 5:30am the stage was 9.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 11.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 10.91 feet is expected at 6:00pm Sunday.
Impacts:
At 11.0 feet: Minor flooding. Lowland overflow. Bridge at
Industrial Way overtopped. Trails and bridges in Watson Woods
Riparian Preserve inundated.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Prescott, Chino Valley, Ponderosa Park, Groom Creek, Downtown
Prescott, Potato Patch, Oak Knoll Village, Whipple, Palace
Station, Wildwood Estates, Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University,
Prescott Regional Airport, Prescott Rodeo Grounds, Rancho Vista
Estates, Mt. Union, Goldwater Lake, Willow Creek Reservoir and
Watson Lake.
- This includes the following highways...
State Route 69 between mile markers 293 and 296. State Route 89
between mile markers 303 and 321...and near mile marker 331.
State Route 89A between mile markers 318 and 321.

This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
White Spar Campground, Upper Wolf Creek Group Campground, Lower
Wolf Creek Campground, Wolf Creek Falls, Acker Park, AC Williams
Granite Creek Park, Watson Lake Park and Goldwater Lake Park.

This includes the following swimming holes...
Wolf Creek Falls.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 1 at 1:57AM EDT until November 1 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding, large breaking waves
of 5 to 8 feet, and dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...Through this evening for the High Surf Advisory and
through Monday for the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Rip
Current Risk.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:

feature will add more moisture and support for showers and storms
than recent days. Strong low-level easterly flow will result in bands
of repeated rainfall for isolated to scattered locations. Showers and
storms are expected to be a bit more widespread with higher rain
rates than the past few days.

* WHERE...All of Palm Beach, Broward, and Miami-Dade counties.

* WHEN...From 10 AM EST this morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered area of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

amounts will fall. However, scattered locations across the east
coast may pick up 3 to 5 inches of rain through Monday. Isolated
spots may see accumulations as high as 5 to 7 inches. These
amounts may fall over a window of a few hours. Expected impacts
could be greater than forecast if the heaviest rainfall occurs
near the coast during times of high tide.
